input.rationale: Closed the empty-command question's disposition and recorded a synthesis Fact for the recovery-value handling family, so the four defects this run asserts share one navigable statement with their distinct responsibilities and receipts. No measurement changed.

investigations.hypothesis: The adoption loop takes any reply whose VBallot is at least the running candidate ballot and copies its command into the candidate, so a reply at the same value ballot that carries no command can replace the command the owner itself contributed; because the dispatch fires when the appended replies reach the slow quorum, which reply is adopted last depends on arrival order, and with two empty replies against one command-carrying reply two of the three exercised orders lose the command while the third keeps it.
investigations.discriminator: Whether the remaining three permutations of the three peer replies behave as the trigger position predicts, and whether a scenario with more command-carrying replies than empty ones flips the outcome.

knowledge.statement: In the captured EPaxos package the value a recovery adopts is not protected by the quorum that holds it: four distinct mechanisms of the same recovery path each let a recovering replica end up proposing, and then deciding, a value other than the one its prepare replies carry. (a) startRecoveryForInstance fabricates a value ballot for its own empty state, so the adoption loop skips genuine replies (epaxos/epaxos.go:1145-1165, 1239-1246). (b) A reply whose value ballot is at most the fabricated one is ignored even when it reports the highest accepted value, so a NOOP replaces an accepted value, including one another live replica has already committed. (c) A reply that reports the instance COMMITTED is discarded once its status reaches lb.status, because the pre-accept guard then rejects the remaining replies, so the first recovery attempt stalls until the retry (epaxos/epaxos.go:870-881, 1255-1313). (d) A reply that carries no command decodes as a non-nil empty slice, which the sub-case 5/6 fallback passes to startPhase1 instead of state.NOOP() (epaxos/defs.go:228-235, epaxos/epaxos.go:1307-1311), and which command is adopted is fixed by the replies present when the slow-quorum trigger fires, so arrival order alone can decide whether the owner's command survives. Recovering replicas that already hold the value are not affected by (a)-(b), and the client re-offer protects the single-NOOP case but not the empty-slice case.
knowledge.conditions: N=5, F=2 configuration of the captured snapshot with Thrifty on and IsLeader false at the recovering replica; the instance owner fails inside its accept window and the recovering replica holds the instance without its command, or (for the arrival-order variant) recovers its own instance while replies at the same value ballot differ.

knowledge.assertion: empty slice adopted and passed through with the trigger timing deciding the command
COMMITTED status adopted then later replies discarded
a recovery lacking the command can decide a different value than a live replica's committed value

investigations.question: When a replica that does not itself hold the value recovers instance (replica A, instance i), does the recovery adopt the value that prepare replies report as accepted/pre-accepted, or does it replace that value with a NOOP?
investigations.hypothesis: startRecoveryForInstance sets inst.vbal to the newly tried ballot and puts its own PrepareReply (VBallot = that ballot, Status/Command from its own possibly empty local state) first into lb.prepareReplies; the adoption loop only takes replies with VBallot >= the running candidate ballot, so genuine replies at the real value ballot are skipped and the recovery proceeds to sub-case 6 with a NOOP command.
investigations.discriminator: Whether a permitted execution can reach recovery at a replica whose crtInstance[A] >= i while its own instance holds no command (no pre-accept, e.g. it only received an Accept because the pre-accept peer set and accept peer set differed); and whether the emitted PreAccept after recovery carries Command NOOP while a delivered prepare reply carried the accepted command at a lower vbal.

gaps.question: Does a permitted execution produce a recovery coordinator that knows instance (A, i) (crtInstance[A] >= i) but holds no command for it, so that the fabricated self-reply decides the adopted value? Candidate: an Accept-phase broadcast to a different peer set than the PreAccept broadcast (peer liveness change between the two broadcasts at the leader) lets a replica learn the instance with Status NONE and Cmds nil.

investigations.question: Can a recovering replica that is not the master-designated leader recover an instance whose accepted value sits at a ballot above its own recovery ballot, or does the periodic retry repeat the same rejected prepare with no enabled repair?
investigations.hypothesis: makeBallot gives every non-designated replica a fixed recovery ballot (r.Id for the instance owner, r.Id+N otherwise), so a recovery whose accepting peers have a higher stored bal is rejected on every attempt: each reply returns before the quorum append, no sub-case is dispatched, no further message is emitted, and the periodic retry repeats the identical Prepare ballot; only r.IsLeader (set by the master's BeTheLeader RPC) lets the ballot climb above maxRecvBallot, after which the same call joins the higher ballot and reaches the sub-case dispatch.
investigations.discriminator: Whether two consecutive startRecoveryForInstance calls on a non-designated replica emit the identical Prepare ballot while every matching reply carries the peers' higher stored bal and the replica emits no PreAccept, Accept or Commit for that instance, and whether invoking the target's own BeTheLeader then produces a Prepare ballot above maxRecvBallot that the peers join (producing a matching reply and a dispatched sub-case).

investigations.question: Does a recovery that restarts phase 1 from a replica without the command stall when one of its acceptors reports the instance as COMMITTED, because adopting that status makes the leader discard every later pre-accept reply?
investigations.hypothesis: The restarted phase-1 leader adopts Status COMMITTED from the first reply whose VBallot is high enough, after which the guard at epaxos/epaxos.go:870 rejects the remaining replies, so preAcceptOKs never reaches FastQuorumSize-1 and neither the fast nor the slow commit branch is entered; the proposal stays PREACCEPTED, the instance is not completed, and the executor's retry repeats the same sequence because the peer still reports COMMITTED.

investigations.question: When a recovery replaces the command that a live owner had proposed and accepted locally, does the owner's client request survive through the re-propose path, and does the original instance produce any reply?
investigations.hypothesis: handleCommit re-queues the pending proposals on the owner's ProposeChan and clears them, so the client's request is not silently consumed by the replacement decision, but the original instance produces no reply because replies are emitted only when the state machine executes commands and the executed command is the NOOP.
investigations.discriminator: Whether the owner's propose channel receives exactly the pending proposal with the same command id while the owner's instance ends COMMITTED with the NOOP, and whether the reply writer for that proposal received no bytes.

investigations.question: Can the handlePreAccept branch that writes r.InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][preAccept.Instance].Cmds run in the captured package, so that a recovery message can write the command into another instance's row or panic on a nil slot?
investigations.hypothesis: The branch requires a local instance with Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil, and its write targets the row of preAccept.LeaderId at the instance index, which is a different instance whenever a recovering coordinator is the sender; if reachable, it would overwrite an unrelated instance's command or dereference a nil *Instance.

knowledge.statement: makeBallot assigns the instance owner the ballot equal to its own replica id and any other recovering replica id+N, and advances it in steps of N only while r.IsLeader is true and the candidate is below maxRecvBallot; epaxos.New hardcodes IsLeader false and only the exported BeTheLeader RPC sets it, which the master invokes for the replica it designates. Repeating startRecoveryForInstance without that flag therefore reuses the identical ballot, whereas after the flag is set the same call emits a ballot above maxRecvBallot. For a non-owner, the boundary is the comparison between its fixed id+N ballot and the ballot the accepting peers have stored: id+N below that value is rejected inertly exactly as the owner's ballot is, while id+N above it is joined by the peers and the attempt advances.

result.summary: Closed the empty-command question and recorded a synthesis Fact so the run's recovery-value defects share one navigable statement. All six registered questions now carry an explained disposition with an account tied to retained receipts: the value-adoption defect and its committed-value contradiction, the boundary-measured recovery-authority gate, the per-attempt status-guard stall, the empty-command replacement with its order-dependent outcome and its measured client-contract hole, the client-completion protection that holds for the single-NOOP case, and the refuted wrong-row-write suspicion. The new Fact states the family's four distinct mechanisms in one place with their source anchors, receipts and referenced behaviors - the fabricated self value ballot, the ballot-gated adoption that discards genuine replies, the COMMITTED-status adoption that stalls the first attempt, and the empty (nil-on-the-wire) slice that the sub-case fallback passes through with arrival order deciding the command - and notes which countermeasures do not cover which case: recovering replicas that already hold the value are unaffected by the first two, and the client re-offer protects the single-NOOP case but not the empty-slice case. The question's hypothesis was refreshed to the measured trigger-position explanation and its remaining discriminator narrowed to the three unexercised permutations and a reply set with more command-carrying than empty replies. Nothing measured changed in this turn; the run's accounts, receipts and limits otherwise stand as recorded.

knowledge.statement: handleCommit, for the instance owner only, tests whether the committed command is a single NONE operation and whether the local leader bookkeeping still holds pending client proposals; when both hold it pushes every pending proposal back onto the replica's own ProposeChan and clears lb.clientProposals, so the client request is re-proposed on a new instance instead of being consumed by the committed NOOP. The re-queued proposal keeps the same command id and reply writer, and the new instance's decision and execution deliver the client reply, while the replaced instance itself produces no reply because its proposals were cleared.

knowledge.statement: Every writer of an instance status at or above PREACCEPTED in the captured package installs a non-nil command in the same step: startPhase1 builds the instance with the batch it was given (and state.NOOP() when a recovery has no command), handlePreAccept sets inst.Cmds = preAccept.Command in the same branch that sets PREACCEPTED or PREACCEPTED_EQ, handlePreAcceptReply and handleTryPreAcceptReply copy lb.cmds, which those paths always hold, and handleTryPreAccept sets the command before setting PREACCEPTED. Acceptors that never pre-accepted report status NONE or PREACCEPTED(_EQ) and never ACCEPTED, because handleAccept records only bal, vbal, seq and deps.
knowledge.conditions: The captured snapshot's epaxos package with Thrifty on and IsLeader false, for any instance of any row (epaxos/epaxos.go:751-779, 796-833, 895-960, 1204-1313, 1316-1352).

knowledge.statement: A nil command slice does not stay nil across the wire: PrepareReply.Unmarshal (and the other RPC decoders) allocate the received slice with make([]state.Command, alen1), so a sender that carries no command yields a non-nil empty slice at the receiver. In handlePrepareReply's adoption loop that empty slice is copied into lb.cmds, and the sub-case 5/6 fallback tests only `inst.lb.cmds != nil`, so it passes the empty slice to startPhase1 instead of substituting state.NOOP(); the resulting instance holds an empty (non-nil) command list, which executeCommands accepts because its guard is also a nil test, and handleCommit's re-offer path does not recognise it because that path requires exactly one command with operation NONE. Which command is adopted is decided by the replies present when the slow-quorum trigger fires, so the same reply set can yield different decided commands under different arrival orders.
knowledge.conditions: Recovery whose replies include one from a replica that holds the instance with no command, when that reply's VBallot is at least the running candidate ballot (epaxos/defs.go:228-235, epaxos/epaxos.go:1239-1246, 1291-1296, 1307-1311 and 1090-1099).

knowledge.statement: In the captured EPaxos package the value a recovery adopts is not protected by the quorum that holds it: four distinct mechanisms of the same recovery path each let a recovering replica end up proposing, and then deciding, a value other than the one its prepare replies carry. (a) startRecoveryForInstance fabricates a value ballot for its own empty state, so the adoption loop skips genuine replies (epaxos/epaxos.go:1145-1165, 1239-1246). (b) A reply whose value ballot is at most the fabricated one is ignored even when it reports the highest accepted value, so a NOOP replaces an accepted value, including one another live replica has already committed. (c) A reply that reports the instance COMMITTED is discarded once its status reaches lb.status, because the pre-accept guard then rejects the remaining replies, so the first recovery attempt stalls until the retry (epaxos/epaxos.go:870-881, 1255-1313). (d) A reply that carries no command decodes as a non-nil empty slice, which the sub-case 5/6 fallback passes to startPhase1 instead of state.NOOP() (epaxos/defs.go:228-235, epaxos/epaxos.go:1307-1311), and which command is adopted is fixed by the replies present when the slow-quorum trigger fires, so arrival order alone can decide whether the owner's command survives. Recovering replicas that already hold the value are not affected by (a)-(b), and the client re-offer protects the single-NOOP case but not the empty-slice case.
knowledge.conditions: N=5, F=2 configuration of the captured snapshot with Thrifty on and IsLeader false at the recovering replica; the instance owner fails inside its accept window and the recovering replica holds the instance without its command, or (for the arrival-order variant) recovers its own instance while replies at the same value ballot differ.

knowledge.assertion: empty slice adopted and passed through with the trigger timing deciding the command
COMMITTED status adopted then later replies discarded
a recovery lacking the command can decide a different value than a live replica's committed value
